meanings: (often used with 一[yi1]) a look; a glance

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.

example.fact: Humans have two eyes set at the front of the face, which gives us depth perception by combining each eye's slightly different view.

meanings: abbr. for 書經|书经[Shu1 jing1]
etymologyHint: A mark made by a pen ⺺

components.note: ⺺ — an abstract mark meant to depict strokes made by a writing brush, the origin of 书's meaning 'book, document, letter.'

example.fact: Paper and printing, both essential to making books, were first developed in ancient China.

meanings: abbr. for 非洲[Fei1 zhou1], Africa
etymologyHint: Two bird's wings opposed; two people back-to-back

components.note: Depicts two things splayed apart from each other — such as a bird's two wings, or two people standing back-to-back — later used for the meaning 'not, contrary to.'

example.fact: 非 rarely stands alone in modern Mandarin — it's most often used inside words like 非常 (fēicháng, 'extremely') to intensify an adjective.

meanings: (literary) (conjunction used to express contrast with a previous clause) but; then
etymologyHint: Laws inscribed 刂 on a slate 贝

components.note: 贝 (a shell, an ancient form of currency/valuables) — represents the property or standards that rules protect.
刂 (a knife) — depicts laws being carved or inscribed onto a slate, the source of 则's meaning 'rule, standard.'

example.pinyin: Měi gè yóuxì dōu yǒu guīzé.
example.fact: 则 rarely stands alone in modern spoken Mandarin; it mostly survives in written words like 规则 (guīzé, 'rule') and 原则 (yuánzé, 'principle').

etymologyHint: Words 口 reaching an ear 斤

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.

example.english: I like to listen to music.
example.fact: The human ear can typically detect sound frequencies ranging from about 20 to 20,000 hertz.

etymologyHint: A burning candle; the rays of the sun

components.note: Originally depicted a burning candle or the sun's rays radiating outward — the source of 白's meaning 'white, bright, clear.'

example.fact: Giant pandas are famous for their black-and-white fur, a coloring found in few other bears.

components.note: 卩 (a kneeling figure, related to 'seal') — ties to 却's older sense of a person stepping back or retreating.
去 (qù) gives the sound — 却 is pronounced què, a close match sharing the same initial and a similar vowel.

example.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, què bú shuìjiào.
example.english: He is tired, but doesn't sleep.
example.fact: 却 works like 'but, yet' in English, but it can't start a sentence on its own — it always follows the subject it comments on.

components.note: 田 (field) — relates to 界's original meaning, the boundary line between farm fields.
介 (jiè) gives the sound — 界 is also pronounced jiè, an exact match.

example.fact: 世界 (shìjiè), literally 'boundary of generations,' is the standard Mandarin word for 'world.'

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 达's meaning 'to reach, arrive, achieve.'
大 (dà) gives the sound — 达 is pronounced dá, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.fact: 达 rarely stands alone — it typically pairs with 到 to form 到达 (dàodá) or 达到 (dádào), both meaning 'to arrive, reach.'

etymologyHint: A person 儿 carrying a torch 火

components.note: 儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.fact: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.

example.fact: 放 combines with many words for 'release' in different senses — 放假 (have time off), 放心 (relax), and 放学 (get out of school).

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.

example.fact: Ants can carry many times their own body weight, making them remarkably strong for their size.

etymologyHint: A hungry person卩 kneeling over food 皀; compare 既

components.note: 卩 (a kneeling figure) — a hungry person kneeling down, about to eat.
皀 (a bowl of food) — the meal in front of them, giving 即 its sense of imminent action, 'right away, that is to say.'

example.fact: 即 appears in many formal words for immediacy, such as 立即 (lìjí, 'immediately') and 即将 (jíjiāng, 'about to').

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de xiàng tā māma.
example.fact: Children often resemble their parents because they inherit genes from both.

etymologyHint: A hand 又 trying to grasp at a bird 隹

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'

example.english: Chinese characters are difficult to write.
example.fact: Chinese characters are often challenging for beginners because, unlike an alphabet, each character has to be learned individually.

components.note: Originally a pictograph of a stone altar or ancestral tablet; its later use as the grammatical word 且, 'moreover, and,' has no connection to that original picture.

example.english: He is smart, and moreover hardworking.
example.fact: 且 rarely appears alone in modern Mandarin; it usually pairs with 而 to form 而且 (érqiě), meaning 'moreover, furthermore.'

components.note: 木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有说话的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu shuōhuà de quánlì.
example.english: Everyone has the right to speak.
example.fact: The idea that everyone holds certain basic rights is a core principle behind many countries' laws today.

etymologyHint: Weighing something with your mind 囟 (altered) and heart 心

components.note: An altered form of 囟 (the mind/head) — the seat of thought.
心 (heart) — thinking was pictured as an activity of both mind and heart, giving 思 its meaning 'to think.'

example.fact: 思 rarely stands alone in modern Mandarin — it's most often seen in words like 意思 (yìsi, 'meaning') and 思考 (sīkǎo, 'to think, ponder').

etymologyHint: A man 十 bridging heaven and earth (both 一)

components.note: 十 — traditionally read as a great man standing tall.
一 (the two horizontal strokes) — heaven above and earth below, which the king bridges, giving 王 its meaning 'king, monarch.'

example.pinyin: Wáng shì Zhōngguó hěn chángjiàn de xìng.
example.english: Wang is a very common surname in China.
example.fact: Wang (王) is shared by more people in China than almost any other surname.

components.note: 豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.

example.hanzi: 大象是最大的陆地动物。
example.pinyin: Dàxiàng shì zuì dà de lùdì dòngwù.
example.english: The elephant is the largest land animal.
example.fact: African elephants are the largest land animals alive today.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.
元 (yuán) was the phonetic base; the pronunciation later shifted to wán, so only a partial rhyme remains today.

example.fact: 完 is commonly attached after a verb to show an action is finished, as in 吃完 (chīwán, 'finish eating') or 做完 (zuòwán, 'finish doing').

meanings: to set up; to put in place

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.

example.pinyin: Tā shèjì le yí zuò xīn fángzi.
example.fact: 设 commonly combines with 计 to form 设计 (shèjì), the standard Mandarin word for 'design.'

etymologyHint: A craftsman using an awl 弋 and a measuring square 工

components.note: 弋 (an awl or tool) — one of the craftsman's instruments.
工 (a measuring square) — a tool for making things to a fixed pattern, giving 式 its meaning 'style, form, type.'

example.hanzi: 这是一种新的学习方式。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng xīn de xuéxí fāngshì.
example.english: This is a new way of learning.
example.fact: 式 rarely stands alone — it's mostly seen in compound words like 方式 (fāngshì, 'method') and 正式 (zhèngshì, 'formal, official').

components.note: ⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'

example.fact: Rainbows form when sunlight passes through raindrops and separates into different colors.

components.note: 足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

example.english: The Silk Road was very long.
example.fact: The Silk Road was an ancient network of trade routes connecting China with Europe and the Middle East.

etymologyHint: A private 己 note 讠; 己 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'

example.english: I write a diary every day.
example.fact: 记 combines with 日 to form 日记 (rìjì), the Mandarin word for 'diary,' literally 'daily record.'

meanings: used in 南無|南无[na1 mo2]

components.note: Originally a pictograph of a musical bell or instrument hung in a frame; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional word 南, 'south.'

example.fact: Southern China generally has a warmer, more humid climate than the north.

etymologyHint: Something that everyone is talking 口 about

components.note: 口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn mài hěn duō chǎnpǐn.
example.fact: 品 rarely appears alone — it's typically part of compound words like 产品 (chǎnpǐn, 'product') and 食品 (shípǐn, 'food product').

meanings: to live; to reside; to stay
etymologyHint: A person 亻 who hosts 主; 主 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.fact: Beijing is one of the most populous cities in the world, home to millions of people.

etymologyHint: To speak 口 with the force of an ox 牛

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'

example.pinyin: Tā gàosu wǒ yí gè mìmì.
example.fact: 告 almost always pairs with 诉 to form 告诉 (gàosu), the everyday Mandarin verb for 'to tell.'
Biologists group living things into categories, such as species and genus, based on their shared traits.
求 often combines with other verbs to form words like 要求 (yāoqiú, 'to require, request') and 请求 (qǐngqiú, 'to request').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.

example.english: According to the map, the station is here.
example.fact: 据 is most commonly seen in 根据 (gēnjù, 'according to, based on'), used to introduce the source of information.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.fact: 程 mostly appears in compounds like 课程 (kèchéng, 'course') and 过程 (guòchéng, 'process'), rarely standing alone.

etymologyHint: Two people 匕 sitting back-to-back; phonetic loan for "north"

components.note: 匕 (a person), doubled and mirrored — two people standing back-to-back; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional meaning 'north.'

example.hanzi: 指南针可以帮助我们找到北方。
example.pinyin: Zhǐnánzhēn kěyǐ bāng wǒmen zhǎodào běifāng.
example.english: A compass can help us find north.
example.fact: A compass needle points toward magnetic north, helping people find direction for centuries.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — links 边's meaning to a boundary or edge one moves along.
臱 (biān) gives the sound — 边 is also pronounced biān, an exact match.

example.english: The shop is next to the school.
example.fact: 边 combines with 旁 to form 旁边 (pángbiān), the everyday Mandarin word for 'next to, beside.'

etymologyHint: A person kneeling 匕 before a corpse 歹

components.note: 匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

example.fact: All living things, including plants, need water to survive.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — relates to 张's original meaning 'to draw a bow taut,' extended to 'to open, stretch.'
长 (cháng) gives a sound hint — 张 is pronounced zhāng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yì zhāng zhǐ.
example.english: There is a piece of paper on the table.
example.fact: 张 is a common measure word in Mandarin for flat, sheet-like objects — paper, tables, photos, and even faces (一张脸).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 该's meaning 'ought to, should,' as if reached through spoken agreement.
亥 (hài) gives a sound hint — 该 is pronounced gāi, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant and tone differ.

example.fact: Drinking enough water helps keep the body's cells functioning properly.

meanings: to hand over; to deliver; to pay (money); to turn over

components.note: Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiāo yí gè xīn péngyou.
example.english: I want to make a new friend.
example.fact: 交 appears in words about connection and exchange, such as 交朋友 (make friends) and 交通 (jiāotōng, 'traffic, transportation').

components.note: 见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'
夫 (fū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from guī.

example.fact: 规 combines with 定 to form 规定 (guīdìng), a common Mandarin word for 'rule, regulation.'

example.english: The Great Wall is also called the 'Ten-Thousand-Li Wall.'
example.fact: 长城 is often called 万里长城 ('the ten-thousand-li Great Wall'), a traditional name emphasizing its immense length rather than an exact measurement.

etymologyHint: A hand 又 taking the ear 耳 of a fallen enemy

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'

example.english: I'm going to the bank to withdraw money.
example.fact: 取 is the common Mandarin verb for withdrawing or obtaining something, as in 取钱 (qǔ qián, 'withdraw money') or 取消 (qǔxiāo, 'cancel').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.fact: 拉 is also used for playing string instruments in Mandarin, as in 拉小提琴 (lā xiǎotíqín, 'to play the violin'), because the bow is pulled across the strings.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服是格子花纹的。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì gézi huāwén de.
example.english: This piece of clothing has a checked pattern.
example.fact: 格 appears in 性格 (xìnggé, 'personality') and 格子 (gézi, 'checked/grid pattern'), among many other compound words.

etymologyHint: A king 王 gazing at the moon 月; 亡 provides the pronunciation

components.note: Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'

example.english: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
example.fact: 望 combines with 希 to form 希望 (xīwàng), one of the most common Mandarin words for 'to hope.'

components.note: 见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhè běn shū hěn yǒuqù.
example.english: I think this book is very interesting.
example.fact: 觉 is pronounced jué in 觉得 (juéde, 'to feel/think') but jiào in 睡觉 (shuìjiào, 'to sleep') — a common case of a character with more than one reading.

meanings: various genera of flowers of Asteracea family (daisies and chrysanthemums), including Atractylis lancea

example.english: Painting is a kind of art.
example.fact: 术 appears in words about skill and craft, such as 艺术 (yìshù, 'art') and 技术 (jìshù, 'technology, skill').

components.note: 页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.fact: 领 combines with 导 to form 领导 (lǐngdǎo), the standard Mandarin word for 'leader' or 'to lead.'

etymologyHint: Two hands 八 holding one object 廾

components.note: 八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'

example.english: How much are these things altogether?
example.fact: 共 combines with 一 to form 一共 (yígòng), a common Mandarin phrase meaning 'in total, altogether,' often used when adding up a price.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.

example.pinyin: Nǐ de dá'àn shì zhèngquè de.
example.fact: 确 pairs with 正 to form 正确 (zhèngquè), the standard Mandarin word for 'correct, accurate.'

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì Zhōngguó de chuántǒng jiérì.
example.english: This is a traditional Chinese festival.
example.fact: Many Chinese festivals, like the Spring Festival, have been celebrated for thousands of years.

etymologyHint: To skillfully wield 帀 a knife 刂

components.note: 帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.fact: 师 combines with 老 to form 老师 (lǎoshī), the everyday Mandarin word for 'teacher.'

etymologyHint: To see 见 again 又

components.note: 见 (to see) — the act of looking.
又 (again, or a hand) — looking closely or repeatedly, giving 观 its meaning 'to observe, view.'

example.english: We went to visit the museum.
example.fact: 观 pairs with 参 to form 参观 (cānguān), the standard Mandarin verb for 'to visit (a place), tour.'

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.

example.fact: 清 combines with 楚 to form 清楚 (qīngchu), the common Mandarin word for 'clear, distinct.'

etymologyHint: A mouth 亼 talking about things

components.note: 亼 — traditionally linked to an image of gathering or covering; its original pictorial sense has become obscure, but the character came to mean 'now, the present.'

example.fact: 今 combines with 天 to form 今天 (jīntiān), the everyday Mandarin word for 'today.'

meanings: to cut; to slice; to carve

components.note: 刀 (knife) — relates directly to 切's meaning 'to cut.'
七 (qī) gives a sound hint — 切 is pronounced qiè, sharing the same initial consonant.

example.fact: Apples are one of the most widely grown and eaten fruits in the world.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/enclosure) — relates to 院's meaning 'courtyard, institution,' an enclosed place.
完 (wán) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yuàn.

example.fact: 院 appears in words for large institutional buildings, like 医院 (yīyuàn, 'hospital') and 电影院 (diànyǐngyuàn, 'movie theater').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 让's meaning 'to let, allow, yield,' something granted through spoken permission.
上 (shàng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from ràng.

example.english: The teacher let us go home.
example.fact: 让 is one of the most common Mandarin causative verbs, used to mean 'to let/make someone do something,' as in 让我看看 (ràng wǒ kànkan, 'let me see').

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 识's meaning 'to know, recognize,' knowledge conveyed through words.
只 (zhǐ) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shí.

example.fact: 识 pairs with 认 to form 认识 (rènshi), the common Mandarin verb for 'to know, be acquainted with (a person).'

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 候's meaning 'to wait, time,' as if a person watching and waiting.
矦 (hóu) gives a sound hint — 候 is pronounced hòu, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.english: Now is the time to eat.
example.fact: 候 pairs with 时 to form 时候 (shíhou), one of the most common Mandarin words for 'time, moment.'

etymologyHint: A belt, creasing one's robe above 卅 but not below 巾

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.fact: Carrying an umbrella is a common way to prepare for sudden rain.

etymologyHint: A hand 寸 pointing the way to someplace 巳

components.note: 寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'

example.english: The tour guide led us to visit the Great Wall.
example.fact: The Great Wall is one of the most visited historical sites in China.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 爭, two hands 爪 and 彐 fighting over 亅

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'

example.hanzi: 两个孩子在争一个玩具。
example.pinyin: Liǎng gè háizi zài zhēng yí gè wánjù.
example.english: Two children are fighting over one toy.
example.fact: 争 commonly appears in 竞争 (jìngzhēng, 'to compete') and 争论 (zhēnglùn, 'to argue, debate').

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 游泳是一种很好的运动。
example.pinyin: Yóuyǒng shì yì zhǒng hěn hǎo de yùndòng.
example.fact: Swimming works nearly every muscle in the body and is a popular form of exercise worldwide.

etymologyHint: A person 夭 with a big grin ⺮

components.note: 夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'

example.fact: Laughing can release endorphins, chemicals in the brain that make people feel good.

components.note: A simplified pictograph of a bird's wings spread in flight — the source of 飞's meaning 'to fly.'

example.fact: Birds' ability to fly inspired many early human attempts to build flying machines.

example.english: Today the wind is very strong.
example.fact: Wind is caused by differences in air pressure across the Earth's atmosphere.

etymologyHint: Modern form of 歨; putting one foot 止 in front of the other

components.note: 止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.english: We take a walk after dinner.
example.fact: Walking regularly is one of the simplest ways to stay healthy.

etymologyHint: A hand with a stick 攵 disciplining a kneeling child 己

components.note: 己 (a kneeling child) — the one being disciplined.

components.note: 广 (a wide shelter/roof) — relates to 府's meaning 'government office, mansion,' a large official building.
付 (fù) gives a sound hint — 府 is pronounced fǔ, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiàn le yí zuò xīn qiáo.
example.english: The government built a new bridge.
example.fact: Governments are responsible for building and maintaining public infrastructure like roads and bridges.

etymologyHint: An animal standing straight; 亠 is the head

components.note: 亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.fact: Beijing and Shanghai, two of China's largest cities, are located far apart in different regions of the country.
况 almost always appears in 情况 (qíngkuàng, 'situation') and 何况 (hékuàng, 'moreover'), rather than standing alone.

etymologyHint: Picture of a cross-shaped house or temple

components.note: A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.fact: Asia is the largest and most populous continent on Earth.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 请's meaning 'to request, invite; please,' a spoken request.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 请 is pronounced qǐng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.fact: 请 is placed at the start of a sentence to politely ask someone to do something, as in 请坐 (qǐng zuò, 'please sit') or 请进 (qǐng jìn, 'please come in').

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates to 技's meaning 'skill, technique,' a skill performed with the hands.
支 (zhī) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.

example.pinyin: Xiàndài jìshù fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
example.fact: Technology has advanced rapidly over the past few decades, especially in computers and communication.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — relates to 际's meaning 'border, between,' an edge or boundary marker.
示 (shì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè guójì xuéxiào.
example.fact: 际 pairs with 国 to form 国际 (guójì), the standard Mandarin word for 'international.'

meanings: to weigh in a balance or on a scale

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 约 originally meant 'to bind, tie up,' extending to 'to agree, arrange' and 'approximately.'

example.english: We'll meet at approximately six o'clock.
example.fact: 约 commonly means 'approximately' in words like 大约 (dàyuē), and 'to arrange, agree' in 约会 (yuēhuì, 'appointment, date').

components.note: A pictograph of an altar or offering table used in ancestor worship — presenting offerings extended to 示's meaning 'to show, display, indicate.'

example.fact: 示 pairs with 表 to form 表示 (biǎoshì), a common Mandarin verb for 'to express, indicate.'

etymologyHint: A person 亻 who goes  somewhere 夂 every day 日

components.note: 亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.english: I need to review before the exam.
example.fact: 复 pairs with 习 to form 复习 (fùxí), the standard Mandarin verb for 'to review (one's studies).'

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) gives a sound hint — 病 is pronounced bìng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.fact: Getting enough rest is one of the best ways for the body to recover from being sick.

etymologyHint: To breathe (life, 心) through one's nose 自; 心 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 自 (nose) — the breath passing through.
心 (heart) — the breath of life, giving 息 its meaning 'to breathe; to rest; news.'

example.english: We need to rest a bit.
example.fact: Resting after physical activity helps muscles recover and rebuild.

components.note: 穴 (cave/hole) — 究's meaning 'to explore deeply, investigate' has been linked to exploring a cave.
九 (jiǔ) gives a sound hint — 究 is pronounced jiū, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 科学家在研究这个问题。
example.fact: Scientific research often takes many years of careful study before reaching a clear conclusion.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.

example.fact: Thread and string have been used by humans for tens of thousands of years to make clothing and tools.

components.note: 亻 (a person), shown twice — one person next to another, similar in shape, the source of 似's meaning 'to resemble, similar, like.'

example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè zì hěn xiāngsì.
example.english: These two characters are very similar.
example.fact: 似 pairs with 相 to form 相似 (xiāngsì), the standard Mandarin word for 'similar, alike.'
官 appears in job titles for government roles, such as 警官 (jǐngguān, 'police officer') and 法官 (fǎguān, 'judge').

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.fact: Humans have used fire for cooking and warmth for hundreds of thousands of years.

etymologyHint: Using an axe 斤 to harvest grain 米

components.note: 斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.fact: 断 pairs with 打 to form 打断 (dǎduàn), a common Mandarin verb for 'to interrupt.'

components.note: 米 (grain, especially husked rice) — 精's meaning 'refined, essence, spirit' relates to rice refined to its purest form.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 精 is pronounced jīng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.fact: Exciting sports competitions often draw large crowds of spectators.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 满's meaning 'full,' water filling to the brim.
㒼 (mán) gives a sound hint — 满 is pronounced mǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Bēizi lǐ de shuǐ mǎn le.
example.english: The water in the cup is full.
example.fact: When a cup is filled to the very top, any more liquid added will simply spill over.

etymologyHint: A hand 又 holding a branch 十 for support

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out for support.
十 (a branch) — held in the hand, the image of support giving 支 its meaning 'to support, prop up; branch.'

example.fact: 支 is a common measure word for long, thin objects in Mandarin, such as pens (一支笔) and cigarettes (一支烟).

components.note: 见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.

example.fact: Television became a common household technology in many countries during the mid-twentieth century.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 消's meaning 'to disappear, dissolve,' like something dissolving in water.
肖 (xiào) gives a sound hint — 消 is pronounced xiāo, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.fact: Clouds form when water vapor in the air condenses into tiny droplets, and they can dissipate as conditions change.

meanings: generic word for peoples or states of south China or south Asia at different historical periods

components.note: 走 (run/walk) — relates to 越's meaning 'to exceed, cross over,' running past a boundary.
戉 (yuè) gives the sound — 越 is also pronounced yuè, an exact match.

example.pinyin: Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng le.
example.english: The weather is getting colder and colder.
example.fact: As winter approaches, temperatures in many places gradually drop.

etymologyHint: Four cooking vessels 口 guarded by a dog 犬

components.note: 口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'

example.pinyin: Gōngchǎng lǐ yǒu hěn duō jīqì.
example.english: There are many machines in the factory.
example.fact: Machines can perform repetitive tasks much faster than humans, which is why factories rely on them.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — 容's meaning 'to contain, hold' relates to a house holding things, extended to 'appearance, to allow, tolerate.'

example.fact: 容 combines with 易 to form 容易 (róngyì), the everyday Mandarin word for 'easy.'

components.note: 灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhāng lǎo zhàopiàn.
example.fact: Photography was invented in the nineteenth century and changed how people record memories.

etymologyHint: Hair 彡 growing on the face 页

components.note: 彡 (hair) — growing hair.
页 (face/head) — hair growing on the face, originally 'beard, whiskers,' later extended to the abstract meaning of 须, 'must, necessary.'

example.fact: 须 pairs with 必 to form 必须 (bìxū), the standard Mandarin word for 'must, have to.'

components.note: A pictograph of a bent arm or elbow; the shape was later borrowed to represent the number 'nine,' unrelated to its original meaning.

example.pinyin: Rénmen shuō māo yǒu jiǔ tiáo mìng.
example.english: People say cats have nine lives.
example.fact: In English, there's a popular saying that cats have nine lives, referring to their remarkable ability to survive dangerous falls and situations.

meanings: (bound form) to increase; to augment; to add to

components.note: 土 (earth) — relates to 增's meaning 'to increase, add,' piling up earth to increase height.
曾 (céng) gives a sound hint — 增 is pronounced zēng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这个城市的人口在增加。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de rénkǒu zài zēngjiā.
example.fact: Many cities around the world have seen their populations grow steadily over the past century.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 研's meaning 'to grind, study closely' relates to grinding a stone to refine or research something.
开 (kāi) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from yán.

example.hanzi: 科学家研究恐龙的历史。
example.english: Scientists research the history of dinosaurs.
example.fact: Dinosaurs lived on Earth for over 100 million years before going extinct.

meanings: used in 寫意|写意[xie4 yi4]

example.fact: Before smartphones and email, people often wrote letters to communicate over long distances.

meanings: to fit; to match; to suit

example.fact: 称 combines with 呼 to form 称呼 (chēnghu), the Mandarin verb for 'to address someone by a name or title.'

meanings: (bound form) to stand on tiptoe and look; to anticipate; to look forward to
(bound form) company; firm; enterprise; corporation (abbr. for 企業|企业[qi3 ye4])
etymologyHint: A man 人 on his feet 止; 止 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 人 (a man) — the figure straining upward.
止 (feet) — standing up on his feet, or toes, to look into the distance, the image of anticipation giving 企 its meaning 'to look forward to, hope for' and, by extension, 'enterprise' (企业).

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì jiā dà qǐyè.
example.fact: 企 pairs with 业 to form 企业 (qǐyè), the standard Mandarin word for 'enterprise, business, company.'

components.note: Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'

example.fact: August falls during summer in the Northern Hemisphere, but winter in the Southern Hemisphere.

etymologyHint: Results produced by capable 力 labor 工; 工 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'

example.fact: 功 pairs with 成 to form 成功 (chénggōng), the standard Mandarin word for 'success, to succeed.'

meanings: used in 嗎啡|吗啡[ma3 fei1]

components.note: 口 (mouth) — relates to 吗's role as a spoken question particle.
马 (mǎ) provides the base sound, though 吗 is usually spoken with a neutral, unstressed tone.

example.fact: 吗 is placed at the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question, as in 你好吗? (Nǐ hǎo ma?, 'How are you?').

etymologyHint: To swaddle 勹 a baby 巳; 勹 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'

example.fact: Bread is one of the oldest and most widely eaten foods in human history.

etymologyHint: Half of a tree trunk; compare 爿

components.note: A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.pinyin: Wǒ chī le yí piàn miànbāo.
example.english: I ate a slice of bread.
example.fact: 片 is a common Mandarin measure word for thin, flat things, such as slices of bread or leaves.

meanings: title of an official historian in ancient China
etymologyHint: A hand 乂 using a pen to record a history

components.note: 乂 (a hand holding a writing tool) — the act of recording events, giving 史 its meaning 'history, chronicle.'

example.fact: 历史 (lìshǐ), the Mandarin word for 'history,' combines 历 ('to pass through, experience') with 史 ('records, chronicle').

example.hanzi: 学校有一个学生委员会。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǒu yí gè xuésheng wěiyuánhuì.
example.english: The school has a student committee.
example.fact: 委 rarely stands alone in modern Mandarin — it's most often seen in 委员会 (wěiyuánhuì, 'committee') and 委托 (wěituō, 'to entrust').

meanings: (classical particle similar to 於|于[yu2]) in

example.fact: 乎 is a classical Chinese particle that survives today mainly in words like 似乎 (sìhū, 'it seems') and 几乎 (jīhū, 'almost').

example.english: I am looking something up in the dictionary.
example.fact: Dictionaries help people find the meaning, pronunciation, and usage of unfamiliar words.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.

example.fact: Materials like foam and certain plastics are designed to be lightweight while still being strong.
